funFact: Baby snakes can slither from the moment they hatch — no lessons needed!
story: A tiny baby snake peeked out of its egg for the very first time and lifted its head to see the big, bright world.
description: Lie on your tummy, little snake! 🐍 Put your hands under your shoulders. Now peek your head and chest up just a tiny bit — sssss! Keep your elbows bent and your tummy on the floor.

funFact: A real cobra can lift a third of its body straight up into the air!
story: In a sunny jungle, a friendly cobra rose up tall to say good morning to the sun and all the parrots cheered.
description: Lie on your tummy with hands under your shoulders. 🐍 Press down gently and lift your chest up like a proud cobra. Keep your hips on the floor and your shoulders away from your ears. Hisss hello to the sun!

funFact: The Great Sphinx in Egypt is over 4,500 years old and as long as three school buses!
story: The mighty Sphinx sat perfectly still in the desert, guarding a secret treasure and smiling a mysterious smile.
description: Lie on your tummy and prop up on your elbows, like a statue in the sand. 🦁 Elbows under shoulders, forearms flat like sled rails. Lift your heart, look ahead, and hold your mysterious Sphinx smile. Shhh... what's your secret?

benefits: Pairs with Cow for a fun flow
funFact: Cats arch their backs to look bigger — and to get a super satisfying stretch!
story: A fluffy kitten woke up from a nap, arched its back way up high, and let out the biggest, squeakiest meow.
description: Come to hands and knees like a table. 🐱 Now breathe out and arch your back way up to the sky — round like a Halloween cat! Tuck your chin and MEOW! Then get ready to flow into Cow.

benefits: Pairs with Cat for a fun flow
funFact: Cows have best friends and get happier when they're together!
story: A cheerful cow stretched in the morning meadow, dipped her belly low, and mooed hello to her best cow friend.
description: Stay on hands and knees, table-top strong. 🐄 Breathe in, let your belly sink down, and lift your chest and tail up. Look gently forward and give us a big happy MOOO! Flow back and forth with Cat.

funFact: Puppies do this exact stretch when they wake up — vets call it the play bow!
story: A sleepy puppy stretched its paws waaay out front, melted its heart to the floor, and wagged its tail at a butterfly.
description: Start on hands and knees, little puppy. 🐶 Keep your hips high and walk your paws far forward. Let your chest melt down toward the floor like warm honey. Rest your forehead down and breathe — ahhh!

funFact: The longest bridge in the world is over 160 kilometers long — that's a lot of bridge!
story: The river was too wide for the little ants to cross, so a kind giant made a bridge with their body and the ants marched across cheering.
description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat near your bottom. 🌉 Press your feet down and lift your hips up, up, up! Keep your knees pointing forward and your arms strong by your sides. You're a bridge — who's crossing over?

funFact: Even tiny bridges matter — some are built just for squirrels and frogs to cross roads safely!
story: A little bridge over a tiny stream lifted just a smidge so one small snail could slide underneath. The snail said thank you very slowly.
description: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. 🌁 Press your feet down and lift your hips just a little — a teeny tiny bridge! Can a pretend snail scoot under you? Lower down soft and slow.

funFact: Resting poses help your body grow — a lot of growing happens while you rest!
story: The bridge worked hard all day letting wagons cross, so at night a soft cloud floated underneath to hold it up while it dreamed.
description: Lie on your back, knees bent, and lift your hips. 🛏️ Ask a grown-up to slide a cushion or block under your bottom. Now rest on your cloud! Breathe slow and let your whole body go soft.

funFact: Some fish sleep with their eyes open because they don't have eyelids!
story: A dreamy fish found a soft patch of sea sponge, floated on top of it, and watched the moonlight sparkle on the waves.
description: Put a cushion or rolled blanket behind you. 🐟 Sit in front of it and gently lie back so your chest lifts like a floating fish. Let your arms rest open like fins. Breathe big fishy bubbles — blub blub!

funFact: A rainbow is really a full circle — from an airplane you can see the whole ring!
story: After the rain, the sky felt plain, so all the kids in town stretched into arches and painted a people-rainbow from hill to hill.
description: Stand tall and sweep your arms up high. 🌈 Press your hips gently forward and arch back just a little, like a colorful rainbow. Reach your fingers to paint red, orange, yellow across the sky! Come up slowly — ta-da!

funFact: Seals clap their flippers underwater to talk to each other!
story: A cheerful seal popped up onto a sunny rock, lifted its chest high, and clapped for every wave that rolled by.
description: Lie on your tummy and press up on your hands like a seal on a rock. 🦭 Lift your chest tall but keep your hips heavy. Now bark like a happy seal — arf! arf! — and wobble your head hello.

funFact: Looking up at the sky and opening your chest can actually make you feel braver!
story: The town clock stretched backward at noon to watch a hot air balloon drift right over its tower.
description: Stand strong with feet hip-width apart. 🙆 Put your hands on your lower back like a shelf. Lift your chest to the sky and lean back gently — just a little! Look up... wow, what do you see up there?

funFact: Dogs stretch like this after naps to get their zoomies ready!
story: A brave dog finished its nap, stretched its chest to the sky, and spotted a squirrel — adventure time!
description: Lie on your tummy, hands by your ribs. 🐕 Press up strong so your arms are straight and your chest shines forward. Roll onto the tops of your feet and lift your knees off the floor. Happy dog face — woof!

funFact: A grasshopper can jump 20 times the length of its own body!
story: A little grasshopper practiced lifting off the leaf every morning, dreaming of the day it would make its biggest jump ever.
description: Lie on your tummy, arms by your sides. 🦗 Breathe in and lift your head, chest, arms, AND legs off the floor — you're flying low like a grasshopper about to jump! Keep looking down at the floor so your neck stays happy. Boing!

funFact: Grasshoppers hear with tiny ears on their bellies!
story: The littlest grasshopper couldn't lift both legs yet, so it lifted one at a time — and that worked perfectly.
description: Lie on your tummy with your chin resting down. 🦗 Keep both hips on the floor and lift just one leg up straight and strong. Hold it... hold it... and float it down. Now the other leg's turn!

funFact: Airplanes tilt their wings to turn — pilots call it banking!
story: Flight 123 zoomed down the runway, spread its shiny wings wide, and lifted off over a sea of fluffy clouds.
description: Lie on your tummy and stretch your arms out to the sides like airplane wings. ✈️ Lift your chest, wings, and legs off the floor. Tilt gently side to side to steer — nyeeeoow! Ready for landing? Float down slow.

funFact: An archer's bow bends but never breaks — that's what makes it springy and strong!
story: An archer in a magical forest bent her bow into a perfect curve, and instead of an arrow, she launched a wish into the sky.
description: Lie on your tummy and bend your knees. 🏹 Reach back and grab your ankles — got them? Now kick your feet into your hands and let your chest lift up. You're a bendy bow ready to launch a wish — whoosh!

benefits: Strengthens one side at a time
funFact: Practicing one side at a time helps your brain learn moves twice as well!
story: The young archer practiced with half a bow first, one side at a time, until both arms were ready for the real thing.
description: Lie on your tummy. 🏹 Reach back with one hand and catch that same-side ankle. Kick your foot into your hand and lift your chest. Stretch your other arm forward like an arrow! Then switch sides.

funFact: Horses can sleep standing up, but they only dream lying down!
story: A toy rocking horse came alive at midnight and rocked back and forth so joyfully that all the other toys lined up for a ride.
description: Lie on your tummy, grab your ankles, and lift into your bow shape. 🐴 Now rock gently forward and back — creak, creak, like a rocking horse! Let your breath do the rocking: breathe in to rock back, out to rock forward. Neigh-heyy!

funFact: Some drawbridges lift one side at a time to let tall ships sail through!
story: The drawbridge lifted one arm high to wave at a passing sailboat, all while holding the road up steady and strong.
description: Lift up into your strong bridge. 🌉 Press one foot down extra hard, then float the other leg straight up to the sky! Keep your hips high and steady like a drawbridge. Switch legs — beep beep, boats coming through!

funFact: A camel's hump stores fat, not water — it's a built-in snack pack for desert trips!
story: A proud camel crossed the golden desert, arched back to drink in the starlight, and knew every dune by heart.
description: Kneel tall with knees hip-width apart. 🐪 Put your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down. Lift your chest to the sky and lean back gently — big camel heart! If it feels easy, reach for your heels. Breathe like the wide desert wind.

funFact: Camels have two rows of super-long eyelashes to keep sand out of their eyes!
story: A young camel learned to lean back one hump at a time, reaching one hoof back while waving the other at the caravan.
description: Kneel up tall, little camel. 🐫 Reach one hand back to touch your heel and stretch your other arm up to the sky. Lift your chest and hold — one-humped camel! Come up slow and switch sides.

funFact: In an old yoga story, a fish listened so well that it learned all the secrets of yoga!
story: A curious fish floated up to the surface, puffed its chest to the sunshine, and listened to the whole ocean humming.
description: Lie on your back with legs long. 🐠 Slide your hands under your bottom, press your elbows down, and puff your chest up high! Let the very top of your head rest light as a feather on the floor. Blub blub — breathe big fish breaths!

funFact: Crabs walk sideways because their knees only bend that way!
story: A sideways-scuttling crab lifted its belly to the sun and challenged the seagulls to a silly dance-off on the beach.
description: Sit with feet flat and hands behind you, fingers pointing toward your toes. 🦀 Press down and lift your hips up to make a table — you're a crab! Lift your chest proud. Want a challenge? Scuttle sideways — snip snap!

funFact: Its Sanskrit name means intense stretch of the east — the front of your body is your east side!
story: A playground slide woke up early, stretched itself long and straight toward the sunrise, and waited for the first happy rider.
description: Sit with legs long and hands behind you, fingers toward your toes. 🛝 Press down and lift your hips until your body is one long, strong slide. Point your toes toward the floor and lift your chest. Wheee — who's sliding down?

funFact: Pigeons puff out their chests to look fancy and to keep warm!
story: A proud pigeon strutted across the town square, puffed up its chest, and cooed the happiest song anyone had ever heard.
description: From hands and knees, slide one knee forward behind your wrist and stretch the other leg long behind you. 🕊️ Press your hands down, sit tall, and puff your chest up like the proudest pigeon in the park. Coo-coo! Then switch legs.

funFact: Every tiger's stripes are unique, just like your fingerprints!
story: A stripy tiger cub practiced its big stretch every morning — one paw kick to the sky — before pouncing through the jungle.
description: Start on hands and knees, strong like a jungle table. 🐯 Kick one leg up and back behind you, bend the knee, and reach your toes toward the sky. Lift your chest and let out a mighty tiger growl — grrr! Switch legs, fierce friend.

benefits: Builds big arm and leg strength
funFact: The first Ferris wheel was so big it could carry 2,000 people at once!
story: At the magic carnival, one brave kid arched into a perfect wheel — and for a second, the whole Ferris wheel spun in their honor.
description: Lie on your back, bend your knees, and plant your feet. 🎡 Put your hands by your ears, fingers pointing to your shoulders. Press up sloooowly — hips high, arms strong — into a big round wheel! Come down gently, chin tucked.
safetyNote: Only try with a grown-up spotter close by. Lift slowly, never crunch your neck, and skip it if your back or wrists hurt today.

funFact: Camatkarasana means the ecstatic unfolding of the enraptured heart — a fancy way to say WOW!
story: One starry night, a kid flipped their downward dog into a shooting-star shape, and the sky sparkled back in applause.
description: Start in side plank on one strong hand. 🌟 Step your top foot behind you onto the floor and lift your hips to the sky. Arch your chest up and reach your free arm overhead like a shooting star — whooosh! Come back the same way you went.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter nearby. Move slowly, keep your neck relaxed instead of dropping it back, and skip it if your wrist or back feels sore.

funFact: This pose is named after Nataraja, the lord of the dance whose dancing is said to keep the whole universe spinning!
story: On a moonlit stage, a dancer balanced on one leg, kicked the other into a beautiful arc, and the audience of fireflies glowed brighter.
description: Stand tall and find a spot to stare at. 🩰 Bend one knee, reach back, and hold the inside of that foot. Kick your foot into your hand so your leg lifts behind you, and stretch your other arm forward. Wobbling is part of the dance!
safetyNote: Practice near a wall with a grown-up spotter. Kick up slowly, keep your chest lifted instead of throwing your head back, and stop if your back pinches.

funFact: Real flying fish can glide over the waves for 200 meters — longer than a soccer field!
story: The bravest fish in the sea flapped its fins, leaped from a wave, and glided over three surprised dolphins.
description: Lie back into your fish pose with your chest puffed high. 🐟 Now lift both legs off the floor and reach your arms toward your toes — you're gliding over the waves! Keep breathing, flying fish. Splash down softly.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter. Keep your neck long and light — no pressing hard on your head — and skip it if your neck or back hurts.

funFact: Sailors long ago thought manatees were mermaids — manatees were very flattered!
story: A mermaid perched on a sparkly rock, curled her tail up behind her, and hooked it in her elbow to wave hello to passing whales.
description: Sit in your pigeon shape, one knee forward, one leg back. 🧜 Bend your back knee and catch that foot in the crook of your elbow — that's your mermaid tail! Reach your other arm up and hold hands behind your head. Lift your heart and sing a sea song!
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter. Warm up your hips and back first, keep your neck soft, and come out slowly if anything pinches.

funFact: Your back has more than 40 muscles working together like a superhero team!
story: When the city needed help, one small hero stretched out on the rooftop, lifted arms and legs high, and zoomed off into the clouds.
description: Lie on your tummy and stretch your arms out front like a flying superhero. 🦸 Breathe in and lift your arms, chest, AND legs as high as they'll go. Hold your flight — whoooosh! Keep your eyes looking down so your neck flies happy.
safetyNote: Lift with a grown-up spotter watching. Keep your neck in line with your spine — no cranking your head up — and rest if your lower back complains.

funFact: The king cobra is the longest venomous snake in the world — but it would rather hide than fight!
story: Deep in the jungle, the king cobra rose taller than all the other snakes, curled its tail toward its crown, and everyone bowed.
description: Start in your tall cobra with arms almost straight. 🐍 Bend your knees and let your toes float up toward the back of your head. Lift your chest royally high — you're the king of snakes! Sssss-spectacular! Lower down slowly.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter after a good warm-up. Lift your chest, not your chin — keep your neck long — and skip it if your lower back or neck hurts.

funFact: Circus performers train for years to bend backward — every big bend starts with a tiny one!
story: The moon leaned back so far one night to see the whole sleeping town at once that it turned into a crescent.
description: Stand with feet wide and strong, hands supporting your lower back. 🌙 Squeeze your legs, lift your chest, and curl back like a crescent moon — a little more than yesterday, never more than feels good. Press through your feet to rise back up. You did it!
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter standing behind you. Bend from your upper back with a long neck, and rise up slowly if you feel dizzy.

benefits: Stretches the front of the legs
funFact: Frogs can't bend their necks, so they swallow by blinking — their eyeballs push the food down!
story: A stretchy frog on a lily pad folded one springy leg up, held its flipper, and got ready for the biggest ribbit-jump of spring.
description: Lie on your tummy and prop up on one forearm like Sphinx. 🐸 Bend one knee and reach back with your other hand to press that foot gently toward your hip. Keep your chest lifted — ribbit! Switch sides, springy frog.
safetyNote: Press your foot gently with a grown-up nearby — never force the knee — and keep your chest tall so your back and neck stay comfy.

funFact: Unicycles are wheels that balance on one point — just like this pose balances on three!
story: The carnival's grand finale: the magic wheel lifted one spoke to the stars and kept on rolling, and the crowd went wild.
description: Press up into your strongest wheel pose first. 🎡 Push down through one foot and both hands, then float the other leg straight up to the sky! Point your toes like a firework. Set it down softly and come down chin-tucked.
safetyNote: Advanced pose — only with a grown-up spotter holding your back, after warming up. Keep your neck relaxed and come down right away if your spine or wrists feel strained.

funFact: Royal pigeons really existed — kings once used them to carry secret letters across kingdoms!
story: The pigeon king arched his feathers into a perfect crown, touched his toes to his head, and every bird in the kingdom cooed in wonder.
description: Sit in pigeon, one knee forward and one leg back. 🕊️ Bend your back knee, reach both arms up and over, and hold your foot behind your head like a feathery crown. Lift your royal heart high! Coo... and gently let go.
safetyNote: Advanced pose — only with a grown-up spotter after a long warm-up. Keep your neck long, never yank your foot, and come out slowly if your back or hips pinch.

funFact: Pigeons can find their way home from over 1,000 kilometers away — built-in GPS!
story: At the royal bird parade, the bravest pigeon bowed all the way backward until its crown touched its tail feathers, and the trumpets sang.
description: Kneel tall like camel pose, hips over knees. 🕊️ With your grown-up helping, arch slowly back and walk your hands down toward your feet. Let your elbows land and your chest bloom to the sky. Breathe big, brave bird! Come up the slow way you went in.
safetyNote: Advanced pose — only with a grown-up spotter guiding your whole descent. Warm up first, keep your neck supported and long, and stop the moment your spine feels crunchy.

funFact: In the full version of this pose, your body makes a shape like a dancer's spinning ribbon!
story: The greatest dancer in the kingdom reached both arms overhead, caught her flying foot, and froze in a shape so beautiful the fountains stopped to watch.
description: Stand on one strong leg and kick the other up behind you. 💃 Reach both arms up and over your shoulders to hold your foot with both hands — a royal ribbon shape! Fix your eyes on one spot and breathe like a calm champion. Release slowly and bow, superstar.
safetyNote: Advanced pose — only at a wall with a grown-up spotter. Keep your neck long and your chest lifting, and hop out gently if your balance or back says enough.

funFact: Lotus flowers sleep underwater at night and pop back up to bloom every morning!
story: A wise old fish tucked its fins into a lotus flower, floated on its back under the pink sunrise, and hummed with the whole sea.
description: Sit and cross your legs into lotus, each foot resting on the other thigh. 🐠 Lean back on your elbows and puff your chest up high, letting the top of your head rest featherlight on the floor. Hold your toes and float, flowery fish! Unfold gently.
safetyNote: Advanced pose — only with a grown-up spotter and warmed-up hips. Keep weight off your head and neck, never force your knees, and unfold right away if anything hurts.
